newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuelan bolivar slips as dollar demand grows.
newsitem.headline: Venezuelan bolivar slips as dollar demand grows.

text.p: The Venezuelan bolivar slipped to 477.75/479.00 per dollar Thursday, compared to 477.25/478.50 per dollar Wednesday, in strong dollar demand driven by high levels of liquidity and low interest rates, traders said.
Foreign currency demand was largely covered by the Central Bank until late in the afternoon when the rate moved slightly as buyers chased sellers.
"The market was strong with plenty of (foreign currency) demand," brokers said.

With money markets awash with excess liquidity and yields on the Central Bank's benchmark six-month monetary stabilization, or TEM, bills falling Wednesday, demand for foreign currency has risen significantly in recent days, traders said.
Currency demand was expected to continue strong Friday with the exchange rate's movement dependent on the Central Bank's response, they added.
